# Viam

> Viam is a platform for building, operating, and managing robots and other machines. A machine runs viam-server, exposes its hardware and services through typed gRPC APIs, and can be discovered, observed, and operated from the CLI, from SDKs, or from an AI agent holding an API key.

## Start here for agents

- [Use Viam from an AI agent](https://docs.viam.com/build-apps/use-viam-from-an-agent/): What an AI agent needs to know to discover, observe, and operate a Viam machine safely: the model, the ways in, and the rules that keep a robot safe when the agent is driving.
- [Drive a machine from the CLI](https://docs.viam.com/cli/drive-a-machine/): Discover, observe, and operate any Viam machine with the CLI alone: list its resources, read its cameras and sensors, plan motion, and stop it, with one key and no SDK code.
- [CLI reference](https://docs.viam.com/cli/reference/): Complete command reference for the Viam CLI: every command, subcommand, flag, and alias.

## Reference

Two distinct reference types share this section: **API reference** (client library methods called from code, e.g. "Component APIs overview") and **configuration reference** (JSON used to configure a resource on a machine, e.g. "Services reference"). Match the entry to what you're actually doing.

- [Component APIs overview](https://docs.viam.com/reference/apis/components/overview/): Scan every Viam component API and its methods at a glance, with links to each method's reference.
- [Service APIs overview](https://docs.viam.com/reference/apis/services/overview/): Scan every Viam service API and its methods at a glance, with links to each method's reference.
- [Manage machines with Viam's machine management API](https://docs.viam.com/reference/apis/robot/): How to use the machine API to monitor and manage your machines.
- [Manage your fleet with Viam's fleet management API](https://docs.viam.com/reference/apis/fleet/): Use the fleet management API with Viam's client SDKs to manage your machine fleet with code.
- [Built-in components](https://docs.viam.com/reference/components/): Configuration reference for Viam's built-in components: per-component models, attributes, and JSON templates.
- [Services reference](https://docs.viam.com/reference/services/): Configuration reference for Viam built-in services: per-service models, attributes, and JSON templates.
- [Full site structure (JSON)](https://docs.viam.com/sitetree.json): every page reachable from the site's main navigation, with hierarchy, always current. Pages hidden from navigation (`toc_hide: true`) are not included -- tutorials are the main case, listed in the catalog below instead. Anything else hidden from navigation isn't intended to be part of the site's structure. Each node has a `title`, and either a `path` (real content, safe to fetch) or a `redirect` (a signpost pointing to the page a human actually lands on -- skip fetching this one); an optional `description`; and an optional `children` array of nested nodes in this same shape.

## Guides

- [Set up your first machine](https://docs.viam.com/set-up-a-machine/first-machine/): Create a machine in the Viam app and install Viam on your compute device.
- [Build apps](https://docs.viam.com/build-apps/overview/): Build software that uses a Viam SDK to talk to your machines and the Viam cloud, from web dashboards to long-running backend services.
- [Motion planning](https://docs.viam.com/motion-planning/): Plan and execute collision-free movements for robot arms and gantries.
- [Build and deploy modules](https://docs.viam.com/build-modules/overview/): Understand the two kinds of modules and how to extend your machine with custom hardware drivers and application logic.

## Full text

- [Full text of agent-first pages](https://docs.viam.com/llms-full.txt): the pages above flagged for full inclusion, concatenated in one file.

## Tutorials

- [Tutorials catalog](https://docs.viam.com/tutorials/catalog.md): worked examples and walkthroughs, several hosted outside this site. Not part of the site structure above, but useful if you're looking for an example that matches what you're building.

## Markdown availability

Every published page on this site also serves a Markdown version: drop the trailing slash from the page's URL and append `.md`. For example, the page at `https://docs.viam.com/reference/components/board/` is also available as `https://docs.viam.com/reference/components/board.md`. This works uniformly for every page, including section landing pages.

Links inside these Markdown files are always absolute, never relative, so they resolve correctly regardless of where you fetched the page from.

Most page content converts cleanly to Markdown syntax (headings, links, lists, bold, code). A minority of pages retain some embedded raw HTML for specific UI widgets (tabbed instructions nested inside step-by-step tables, glossary term tooltips, images, and card grids) rather than force-converting them — this HTML is valid inside a Markdown document and reads fine for both humans and machine readers; it just isn't pure Markdown syntax in those specific spots.

Code samples are unaffected by this: they're always in real fenced code blocks with the correct language tag and exact original whitespace, never flattened or re-escaped.
